chapter_seo_title: Desolate Era Ch 291: Ji Ning Arrives at the Grand Xia Imperial Capital – Yinglong Guard & Heaven-Mang Hall
chapter_meta_description: Ji Ning brazenly returns to Anchan and teleports to the Grand Xia Imperial Capital, where he witnesses the towering Yinglong Divine Mountain, the majestic Heaven-Mang Hall, and four terrifying Fiendgod gatekeepers.
og_title: Desolate Era Ch 291: The Grand Xia Imperial Capital
og_description: Ji Ning walks openly into an ambush, teleports to the dynasty's heart, and gets his first overwhelming look at the Heaven-Mang Hall and its Fiendgod guardians.
twitter_description: Ji Ning strolls into the Grand Xia Imperial Capital without a disguise, mentally dominating the Shaoyan clan's lookout and taking in the jaw-dropping scale of the Heaven-Mang Hall.

lore_anchors.definition: The ten-thousand-li-tall magic-treasure mountain that serves as the headquarters of the Yinglong Guard; the tallest structure in the Grand Xia Imperial Capital, deliberately built taller than the Emperor’s own palace.

The nine-thousand-nine-hundred-ninety-nine-li-tall magic-treasure palace of the Grand Xia Emperor, radiating multicolored light and featuring nine layers of clouds, the first of which are red clouds at six thousand li.

The supreme ruler of the Heavenly Court in Daoist cosmology; in Desolate Era, it is implied that mortal-world emperors of major worlds can negotiate with the Celestial Thearch on roughly equal footing.

Four ten-thousand-zhang-tall elemental Fiendgods (Fire, Water, Metal, Darkness) guarding the Imperial City gate, each radiating an aura comparable to the terrifying guardians of the Mount Yujue trial.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Ji Ning show up without any disguise?
cultural_notes_faq.a: To assert psychological dominance. By walking openly into the Shaoyan clan's trap, he signals that he is not afraid and forces them to react on his terms.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the Yinglong Divine Mountain taller than the Emperor's palace?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It hints at the extraordinary, quasi-divine authority of the Yinglong Guard, subtly challenging the normal hierarchical conventions of imperial architecture.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the significance of the Heaven-Mang Hall's nine cloud layers?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They mirror the Nine Heavens of Daoist cosmology, reinforcing the idea that the Grand Xia Emperor rules a realm that rivals the Heavenly Court itself.
